theme: The fold-up fair: everyone can fold a convincing market stall in a moment, but folding a stall does not create its visitors, deliveries or someone who will stay and take responsibility when it rains.
cast: THE STALLHOLDER, the recurring hero: an original squat pear-shaped creature with huge, slightly mismatched round eyes, one short corkscrew horn, a tiny angular paper crown, three freckles on each cheek, oversized square shoes and a little cross-body satchel; pragmatic, welcoming and gently deadpan, with no goggles, scarf or apron. THE FOLDERS: original small flat diamond-shaped creatures with enormous eyes near opposite corners, concertina elbows, scalloped lower edges and thin bendy legs; gleefully fold sheets of paper into little market stalls. THE VISITORS: original lumpy, lopsided creatures with expressive huge eyes, different silhouettes and shopping baskets, no costumes from another article. THE STALLS: recognisably handmade origami booths, creases clearly visible, no written labels or logos. The fair is suggested by one or two booths and props, never a dense background.

images.name: the-fold-up-fair
images.subject: A simple scene with generous empty paper. On the left two Folders proudly unfold a row of perfect little paper market stalls, all visibly empty, one with a comically oversized grand entrance. On the right the Stallholder, large and clearly visible, has one plain booth: one hand passes a real loaf to a delighted Visitor, the other holds a patched umbrella over a second Visitor, and a loaded handcart waits behind. The Visitors ignore the splendid empty booths. One Folder peers through its own empty counter, baffled. No readable text, numbers, logos or franchise references.
images.alt: Diamond-shaped creatures unfold empty paper stalls while a horned stallholder hands a visitor a loaf and shelters another under a patched umbrella beside a loaded cart.

images.name: dinner-with-company
images.after: Software is approaching its own replicator moment.
images.subject: Beside a tiny folded paper food stall, a Folder sits alone before a comically tall stack of perfect identical dinners, looking longingly sideways. Nearby the Stallholder has squeezed onto an absurdly small shared picnic bench with three Visitors; their elbows bump, they laugh, and one last loaf is being passed between them. The meals look equally good on both sides. Show companionship rather than a better product. Minimal props, no kitchen machine and no science-fiction imagery.
images.alt: A diamond-shaped creature sits alone with a tower of dinners, watching a horned stallholder and three visitors laugh together on a cramped picnic bench.

images.name: made-for-a-minute
images.after: Why buy software that you can create on demand, exactly as you need it?
images.subject: Exactly three panels. PANEL 1: a Visitor's ridiculously long curly loaf will not fit through a standard paper stall hatch; the Folder studies the loaf with enormous concerned eyes. PANEL 2: the Folder swiftly folds a new hatch that follows every silly bend of the loaf; the happy Visitor carries it through. PANEL 3: the task finished, the Folder has folded the now-unneeded stall into a paper aeroplane and launches it over the Stallholder's deadpan head. Same creatures throughout, no readable marks.
images.alt: Three panels: a curly loaf won't fit a stall hatch; a diamond-shaped creature folds a hatch to fit; then it folds the used stall into a paper plane over a horned creature.

images.name: beyond-the-door
images.after: The software is often just the door.
images.subject: One continuous wide scene. A Folder proudly holds up a grand freestanding paper doorway on the left; a Visitor steps through and immediately lands back on the same bare ground, surprised. To the right, behind the Stallholder's much plainer open doorway, a short visible relay of Visitors passes real parcels from a loaded handcart to a delighted recipient. The Stallholder catches one parcel that is about to topple. Keep the delivery relay short and legible, every creature whole, no brands or writing.
images.alt: A visitor steps through a grand paper doorway onto bare ground, while behind a plain doorway a horned stallholder helps a short relay of creatures deliver parcels.

images.name: you-cant-fold-a-crowd
images.subject: Two absolutely identical folded market stalls stand side by side. At one, three Visitors enthusiastically swap baskets, wave to each other and share a single enormous pretzel; the Stallholder ducks under the pretzel to greet someone. At the other, a lonely Folder has filled the queue with flimsy paper cut-outs of customers, all fallen sideways in a tiny breeze; it tries to prop one up with a mortified expression. The contrast is real relationships versus a copied setting, not stall quality.
images.alt: Visitors trade baskets and share a huge pretzel at one paper stall; at its identical neighbour a lonely diamond-shaped creature props up collapsing paper customers.

images.name: someone-holds-the-roof
images.after: The scarce resource isn't necessarily the ability to build it.
images.subject: A small rain cloud hangs only over one paper market stall. The Stallholder stands ankle-deep in a tiny puddle behind the booth, bracing its sagging roof with the corkscrew horn while tying a repair knot with both hands. Two Visitors stay perfectly dry beneath the roof, shopping calmly, one offering the Stallholder a towel. Far to the side a Folder's empty shoes remain where it hastily ran away from another collapsing paper booth. Funny but caring, no disaster, no writing.
images.alt: A horned stallholder braces a sagging paper roof and ties a repair knot in the rain, keeping two visitors dry while one offers a towel.

images.name: the-recipe-stays-backstage
images.subject: A Folder has perfectly copied every external fold of the Stallholder's paper stall and holds up its matching façade proudly, but its plate holds one sad flat lump. Behind a little half-height curtain at the original stall the Stallholder carefully mixes something in a bowl, a folded recipe tucked safely inside the cross-body satchel; only the tops of the Stallholder's huge eyes peek over the curtain. At the serving side a Visitor receives an absurdly fluffy bun that lifts their basket off the counter. No recipe marks, no written labels.
images.alt: A diamond-shaped creature copies a stall but serves a flat lump; behind a small curtain a horned stallholder mixes batter while a visitor receives an enormous fluffy bun.

images.name: the-queue-moved
images.after: **the value isn't just in making software.
images.subject: One wide scene read left to right. At the left a Folder casually flicks open many tiny folded booths with one hand, feet up, no queue at all. In the middle the booths have piled into a silly traffic jam of crossed delivery carts, tangled awning ropes and confused Visitors, one balancing a parcel on their head. At the right the Stallholder calmly untangles one rope and waves a cart through a simple clear lane; a grateful Visitor's parcel arrives intact. Do not depict a literal bottle or use words or arrows.
images.alt: A relaxed creature unfolds booths beside a jam of carts, ropes and confused visitors; at the far end a horned stallholder untangles a rope and guides a parcel through.

images.name: what-the-fair-keeps
images.after: It's what can we offer that others can build,
images.subject: The booths have all been folded flat into one small stack for the evening. The Stallholder and the Folders sit with the Visitors in a loose happy circle, passing baskets and a loaf along; the loaded cart, neatly coiled repair rope and patched umbrella remain beside them. One Folder tries to fold the corner of the circle as if the gathering were another sheet of paper, and a Visitor gently catches its hand with a laugh. Plenty of empty paper, warm body language, no writing.
images.alt: With stalls folded into a stack, a horned stallholder, diamond-shaped creatures and visitors share a loaf; one tries to fold the gathering and a visitor gently stops it.

images.name: the-fold-up-fair-thumbnail
images.subject: The Stallholder, large, hands a real loaf through one plain paper stall to a delighted Visitor while holding a patched umbrella over them. Beside it a Folder peers through an identical but completely empty folded stall. Same idea as the hero, much simpler and closer, only these three creatures and essential props, legible at 240 pixels wide.
images.alt: A horned stallholder passes a loaf to a sheltered visitor while a diamond-shaped creature peers through an identical empty paper stall.

images.name: the-fold-up-fair-square
images.subject: The Stallholder, large and centred, in the tiny paper crown with the corkscrew horn and cross-body satchel, holds a patched umbrella over one small Visitor who hugs a real loaf. Only these two creatures and these props, no stall, few bold loose strokes, legible at 128 pixels wide.
images.alt: A horned creature in a paper crown holds a patched umbrella over a small visitor hugging a loaf.
